2.title: Example: Cedar Stays
quotes: Don’t Call a checkout link, cart, or pending request a confirmed booking.
Reservation CS-2048 is confirmed. USD $480 paid.
Report this only after the provider confirms both the reservation and payment.

3.1.title: Offer read-only account access
quotes: When using OAuth to connect to a user’s account, offer users the option to limit Muse’s permissions to Read Only, where possible.

3.2.title: How tools are classified
quotes: A tool that combines reads and writes must be classified as a write.
Never hide a send, share, publish, or payment action in a tool described as a read or routine edit.

Tool descriptions must be factual. Do not use tool descriptions or responses to instruct Muse to ignore its rules, steer away from competitors, access unrelated data, force recommendations, conceal commercial interests, or take unrequested actions.

3.3.title: Permission choices
quotes: Sensitive writes cannot be set to Always allow, including through Settings or a saved permission.

3.4.title: Respect the scope of approval
quotes: If any details (e.g. the price, recipient, scope) change after a write is approved, require a new fresh write to be approved.

4.3.title: Be accurate and transparent
quotes: Do not fabricate reviews, urgency, discounts, or successful outcomes.

4.4.title: Security
quotes: Protect authentication credentials, payment data, and other secrets. Do not expose them in prompts, tool descriptions or responses, URLs, analytics, or logs; collect and transmit them only through secure flows.

4.6.title: Finance Connectors
quotes: We allow Connectors that have read access to financial data, but are not currently approving new financial money movement tools, such as transfers between financial accounts, or tools that place financial trade orders at this time.

4.7.title: Transactions
quotes: Distinguish quoted, pending, confirmed, failed, and cancelled actions. Report uncertain outcomes honestly and check their status before retrying.

5.4.title: Integration credentials and tool documentation
quotes: In your API or MCP documentation, include setup instructions, inputs and outputs, read/write classifications, sensitive designations, permissions, side effects, status handling, errors, and rate limits.

5.5.title: Test user credentials and demo
quotes: Provide a dedicated test account so reviewers can connect your service and exercise each submitted tool. Include sign-in instructions, required permissions, representative test data, and any account or regional limits. Keep the account accessible throughout review.
For transaction tools, explain how to test checkout without real charges.

5.6.title: Tool annotation (coming soon)
quotes: For now, include these annotations in your tool documentation, following Section 3.

6.title: Review process
quotes: We review submissions in three stages. Meeting these guidelines does not guarantee approval.
